<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|142|THE GOSPEL|CHA. II.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=2|verse=48}}† And seeing him, they vvondered. And his mother said to him, Sonne, vvhy hast thou so done to vs? behold thy father and I sorovving did seeke thee. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=49}}† And he said to them, VVhat is it that you sought me? did you not knovv, that I must be about those things, vvhich are my fathers? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=50}}† And they vnderstood not the vvord that he spake vnto them. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=51}}† And he vvent dovvne vvith them, and came to Nazareth: and vvas {{sup|‖}} subiect to them. And his mother kept al these vvordes in her hart. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=52}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} proceeded in vvisedom and age, and grace vvith God and men.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. II.}}}}

''14. Men of good wil.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Free wil.}}The birth of Christ giueth not peace of minde or saluation but to such as be of good will, because he worketh not our good against our willes, but our willes concurring. ''Aug. quæst. ad Simplic. li. 1. q. 2. to. 4''.

''19. Kept al.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Our B. Lady ful of deepe contemplations.}}Our Lady though litle be spoken of her concerning such matters in the Scriptures, because she was a womā, and not admitted to teach or dispute in publike of high mysteries: yet she knew al these mysteries, and wisely noted and contemplated of al those things that were done and said about Christ, from the first houre of his Conception til the end of his life and his Ascension.

''34. To the ruine.''] Therfore to the ruine of some, because they would not beleeue in him, and so vvere the cause of their owne ruine, as he is els where called ''A stumbling stone'', {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Pet. 2, 8''.}}because many would stumble at him and so fall {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Mens ruine and damnation is of them selues.}}by their owne fault. other some he raised by his grace from sinne to iustice, and so he was the resurrection of many. The Apostle vseth the like speache, saying: ''We are to some the odour of life, vnto life: to others, the odour of death, vnto death''. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2. Cor. 2, 16''.}}Not that their preaching was to cause death, but because they that would not beleeue their preaching, wilfully incurred deadly sinne and damnation.

''37. A vvidow.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Holy widowhod.}}Marke that widowhod is here mentioned to the commendation thereof euen in the old Testament also, and the fruite and as it were the profession thereof is here commended, to witte, fasting, praying, being continually in the Temple. euen as S. Paul {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Cor. 7. 1. Tim. 5.''}}more at large for the state of the new Testament speaketh of widowhod and virginitie, as being professions more apt and commodious for the seruice of God.

''37. By fastings and praiers seruing.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Fasting an act of religion.}}Seruing, in the Greeke is λατρεύουσα, that is, doing diuine worship vnto God, as by praier, so also by fasting. so that fasting is λατρεία, that is, an act of religion whereby we doe worship God, as we doe by praier, and not vsed only to subdew our flesh, much lesse (as Heretikes would haue it) as a matter of pollicie.

''51. Subiect to them.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Dutiful obedience to parents.}}Al children may learne hereby, that great ought to be their subiection and obedience to their Parents, when Christ him self, being God, would be subiect to his parents being but his creatures.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The second}} part: The preparation that vvas made to the manifestation of CHRIST.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. III.}}}}}}

{{c|''Iohn, to prepare al to Christ (as Esay had prophecied of him) baptizeth them to penance; 7. insinuating their reprobation, and the Gentils vocation, 10. teaching also and exhorting ech sort to doe their dutie. 15. That him self is not Christ, he sheweth by the difference of their tvvo baptismes: 17. and saith that Christ vvil also iudge his baptized. 19. Iohns imprisonment. 21. Christ being him self also baptized of Iohn, hath testimonie from heauen, 23. as he vvhose generation reduceth vs againe to God.''}}<noinclude>{{rh|||AND}}</noinclude>
